newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI MD sees Ellicott report in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI MD sees Ellicott report in 1997.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said it was unlikely that a report on the heavy engineer's investment in the Holter water treatment business by lawyer Bob Ellicott would be ready until early 1997.

"He is still saying the end of the year but I personally think that is a bit of a stretch given the amount of material that has to be digested," managing director Stancliffe told Reuters in an interview.
ANI said in late September that Ellicott, a former Austalian attorney-general and federal judge, would investigate ANI's acquisition of the now wholly-owned Holter operation.

The appointment rescinded a decision by the ANI board to have two directors, including former dissident shareholder Ross Palmer, investigate Holter and its troubled operations which were at the centre of ANI's A$213.2 million net loss in 1995/96.
Asked when the board was likely to consider the report, Stancliffe said this would probably be in about late January.
Lawyers working with Ellicott returned from Germany in late November after interviewing Holter executives, he said.
They had also spoken to Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press, which was the largest shareholder in ANI when the Holter acquisition began. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
